en.name: NewsBoard
en.short_description: Headlines from BBC News, NPR and The Guardian, sorted by topic.
en.subtitle: Publisher feeds, by topic
en.description:
NewsBoard is a reader for news that other people report. It fetches 23 public news feeds from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian, and shows you what those newsrooms published — their headline, their summary, their byline where they gave one, and the time they published it. NewsBoard writes none of it and changes none of it.

WHERE EVERY STORY COMES FROM
Every article carries the name of the publisher whose feed it arrived in, and opening one gives you a "Read at BBC News" button that takes you to that publisher's own page in your browser. Profile lists all four publishers with a link to each of their sites. If a feed does not supply something — a picture, a byline, a summary — that space is left empty rather than filled in.

BY TOPIC
Technology, business, science, health, politics, sport, entertainment, environment and world, plus a For You view of everything and a Trending view. Trending here means one thing only: the same story is being carried by more than one of the publishers. There is no popularity score, no view count and no ranking, because nothing in the app measures any of those.

READ LATER, FOLLOW, SEARCH
Save any article to read later; saved articles stay on your device. Follow a topic or a hashtag and the Following tab collects matching stories. Search runs across the headlines, summaries, publishers and tags of everything that has loaded.

OFFLINE, HONESTLY
The last set of stories NewsBoard successfully downloaded is kept on the device. With no connection it shows that set and says "Offline · showing stories saved 2h ago" above it, so you always know how old what you are reading is. With nothing downloaded yet it tells you the fetch failed and offers a retry, instead of showing you an empty page that looks like a quiet news day.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
No account, no sign-in. No advertising. No subscription and no in-app purchase — there is no paid tier and nothing is held back. Nothing in NewsBoard is generated: no AI summaries, no rewritten headlines. There is no push notification. Market quotes are not available: opening a stock symbol says so rather than showing a made-up price.

_blocked.feed_licensing: A human has to confirm the app may redistribute these publishers' feeds before it is submitted. The feeds are the publishers' own public RSS, the app shows only the headline, the publisher's summary and a link back, and every item is attributed by name — but BBC and NPR both distinguish personal from business use in their syndication terms, and this is an App Store listing by a company.
_blocked.evidence: mobile/lib/core/data/feed_sources.dart lists 23 feeds across feeds.bbci.co.uk, feeds.npr.org and theguardian.com. mobile/lib/core/data/rss_parser.dart:105-119 keeps the publisher's own title, link, summary, author and date and derives nothing. mobile/lib/features/article/article_screen.dart renders a "Read at <publisher>" button that opens the publisher's page.
_blocked.to_unblock: Get written confirmation for each publisher, or swap the list in feed_sources.dart for feeds whose terms already permit this use. The list is the only place feeds are declared; the fetcher, the Profile credits and the tests all read it.

review_information.notes:
No account and no sign-in anywhere in the app. First launch shows a two-step setup: a language list, then a topic picker that needs at least one topic before "Start reading" is enabled. Nothing else is required.

Where the articles come from: the app fetches 23 public RSS feeds over HTTPS from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian (mobile/lib/core/data/feed_sources.dart). Each article keeps that publisher's headline, link, summary, byline and publication time; a field the feed does not carry is left null rather than filled in. Nothing is bundled in the binary — an earlier build shipped ten invented articles attributed to real newsrooms, and those have been deleted along with the file that held them. The last successful download is cached on the device so the app has something to show offline, with a visible line saying when it was fetched.

Outbound network use is: the 23 feed URLs and the article thumbnails those feeds link to. The app calls AglCrash.init (agl_observability), but no google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist is present in this build, so Firebase never initialises and no crash report is sent. Tapping "Read at <publisher>" or a publisher in Profile opens that page in the external browser.

Things that might otherwise look like defects:
- The Finance chip in the category rail is always empty. None of the configured feeds is mapped to that category; the app shows its normal "nothing here yet" state.
- "NewsBoard Premium" is a single screen that states there is no paid plan. There is no in-app purchase product in this build, no price is shown, and nothing in the app is gated. It is reachable from Profile.
- Opening a stock symbol shows a message that no market-data provider is connected, rather than displaying an invented quote.
- The language picked during setup is saved as a preference, but the app's own screen text is English and articles are in the language the publisher wrote them in.

No ad SDK is linked and the app shows no advertising. Bookmarks, followed topics and theme are stored on the device.
